lines.text: Home electricity prices are up 32% since 2020.
lines.say: Home power prices are up thirty-two percent since twenty twenty.

lines.text: EIA's October energy outlook, with its winter heating forecast, comes out today, Oct 6, around noon Eastern.
lines.say: And the government's new energy outlook, with its winter heating forecast, comes out today around noon Eastern.

scene.headline: EIA energy outlook due at noon ET

lines.text: Average US home price per kWh: 13.15 cents in 2020, 17.3 cents in 2025.
lines.say: The average US home paid about thirteen cents per kilowatt-hour in twenty twenty. In twenty twenty-five, about seventeen.

lines.text: Example: a home using 1,000 kWh a month paid about $132 in 2020 and $173 in 2025.
lines.say: For example, a home using one thousand kilowatt-hours a month went from about one hundred thirty-two dollars to one hundred seventy-three.

lines.text: EIA's September 2026 forecast: 18.2 cents per kWh in 2026.
lines.say: And the September forecast from the EIA puts it at eighteen point two cents for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: EIA expects record US power use in 2026, driven by data centers and factories.
lines.say: Part of the story is demand. The EIA expects record power use, driven by data centers and factories.

lines.text: A power bill is the price per kWh times how many kWh you use. Households don't set the price; usage is the part they see and control.
lines.say: Your bill is just price times usage. Nobody at home sets the price, so usage is the part a household actually controls.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Home power prices are up 32% since 2020. Here's the math.
post.ig:
Home electricity prices are up about 32% since 2020.
Average US home price: 13.15 cents per kWh in 2020, 17.3 cents in 2025 (EIA).
Example: 1,000 kWh a month went from about $132 to $173.
EIA's Sept 2026 forecast: 18.2 cents in 2026, with record power use driven by data centers and factories.
EIA's October outlook and Winter Fuels Outlook come out Oct 6, 2026.
Sources: EIA Electric Power Annual Table 2.4; EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook, Sept 2026.
